rule: Casual leave reduced from 12 to 10 days per year
v2_text: Employees at NovaTech Solutions are entitled to 10 casual leave (CL) days per calendar year, credited at 10 days per year in equal monthly instalments. Casual leave can be used for short personal matters and should ideally be applied for at least 1 day in advance through the HR portal, except in genuine emergencies. A maximum of 3 consecutive CL days can be taken at a stretch; anything longer should be applied as earned leave. Unused casual leave does not carry forward to the next year and is not encashable. Please ensure your manager approves the leave request before your planned time off to avoid attendance discrepancies.

rule: Expense claim submission window extended from 30 to 45 days
v2_text: Eligible business-related expenses, such as internet bills for remote work, mobile phone usage, and approved client entertainment costs, can be reimbursed through the HR/finance portal. To claim reimbursement, submit original receipts along with a completed expense form within 45 days of incurring the expense. Reimbursement requests are reviewed by your manager and processed by the finance team within 10 business days of approval, credited directly to your registered bank account. Certain reimbursements, like internet allowances, may have monthly caps as defined in your compensation structure. Please retain all receipts, as claims without valid proof of expense cannot be processed.

rule: Notice period for employees who completed probation reduced from 60 to 45 days
v2_text: The standard notice period at NovaTech Solutions is 45 days for employees who have completed probation, and 15 days for those still on probation, as specified in your employment agreement. During the notice period, you're expected to continue performing your regular duties, complete handover documentation, and support the transition of your responsibilities. If you wish to leave earlier than your notice period allows, you may request a reduced notice period or buyout option, subject to manager and HR approval, where the shortfall may be adjusted against your final settlement or paid by you. Extensions to the notice period are rare and only considered in exceptional business-critical situations.
